description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-04: the 1D drift-flux and 6-equation models are 'the bread and butter of tampines before the AI is in... Before PINNs and other AI accelerations of the solver are in.'

This bead exists to hold the AI stage OPEN BUT LAST, so the 'Artificial-intelligence' in the TAMPINES acronym does not get built before the thing it is supposed to accelerate.

HARD ORDERING: the deterministic 1D solvers (op-dt3.12 drift-flux, op-dt3.13 two-fluid, on the op-dt3.18 HEM baseline) must exist and be V&V'd FIRST. They are the reference a surrogate is measured against; a PINN with no verified baseline cannot be validated at all.

When this is picked up, the workspace V&V rule applies with full force: a surrogate must document methodology AND measured results (error vs the deterministic solver over a stated input domain, with uncertainty), and must state where it is NOT valid. Per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md this remains education/research/V&V only -- never operational or safety-critical.
title: tampines: PINN / AI acceleration of the 1D solvers — explicitly AFTER the deterministic baseline

description: Give a surface thickness: offset a copy of every vertex inward along its area-weighted vertex normal by 'thickness', add the inner shell with reversed winding (cavity-facing), and bridge open boundary edges with rim quads. Blender analogue: MOD_solidify (simple mode). Turns a surface patch into a volume (CFD wall meshing) or a closed mesh into a hollow shell. Reuses the boundary directed-edge tracing from fill_holes and consistent-winding rules. New MeshOp::Solidify { thickness } variant. V&V: open grid -> closed slab chi=2, watertight; closed cube -> nested outer+inner shells (hollow box) chi=4, each shell watertight; thickness=0 collapses inner onto outer.
title: outram-blender: solidify (shell thickness -> closed solid)

acceptance_criteria: The four kovan search crates cargo-check on both host and aarch64-linux-android with the project toolchain.
description: cargo check of kovan-discovery / kovan-semantics / kovan-cli / kovan-literature fails to resolve because transitive dep kstring@2.0.3 declares rust-version 1.96.0 while the build toolchain is rustc 1.94.1. Pulled in via the gix/grep (gitoxide + ripgrep) dependency chain used for git-awareness + text search. NOT Android-specific — reproduces identically on the host target. Options: (a) bump the pinned/CI rustc to >=1.96, or (b) pin kstring to the latest 1.94.1-compatible version via 'cargo update kstring@2.0.3 --precise <ver>'. Blocks the Android/Termux portability sweep (op-zfr.6) for those 4 crates until resolved.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Confirmed 2026-07-21: 'cargo update -p kstring --precise 2.0.2' (2.0.3->2.0.2, 116 deps unchanged) resolves cleanly under rustc 1.94.1 and unblocks all 6 kovan crates (cli/tui/discovery/semantics/literature/[+ any]) on both host and aarch64-linux-android. So fix option (b) pin-kstring-2.0.2 is verified working; option (a) is bump build toolchain to >=1.96 (the maintainer's machine already has that, since 2.0.3 is in Cargo.lock). Maintainer's call which to adopt.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: RESOLVED on develop (merged via outram-foam, commit pins kstring 2.0.2 in Cargo.lock for the rustc-1.94 MSRV). Verified 2026-07-24: kovan-cli, kovan-tui, kovan-discovery, kovan-semantics, kovan-literature all build on BOTH host and aarch64-linux-android --all-targets under rustc 1.94.1. The whole non-GUI workspace now compiles on Android. Suggest close.

title: kstring@2.0.3 MSRV (needs rustc 1.96) blocks kovan search crates on rustc 1.94.1

description:
Survey (2026-08-17) found this piece already done: src/opcua_core/ (extracted from
ciet_opcua under op-szmi.1, Done) provides a reactor-agnostic, enum-dispatched
OpcuaSimulator/OpcuaVariable trait pair (no dyn), a generic spawn_opcua_server_thread,
PKI path helper, and mDNS discovery (advertise + browse). src/ciet_opcua/ is the fully
worked reference implementation (2965 lines, 37 tests) backing ciet_educational_simulator_v2
+ the standalone ciet_v2_opcua_client bin + tests/ciet_v2_headless_remote_control.rs.
src/htgr_opcua/ has its node maps (HtgrSignal/HtgrControl) and state snapshot but is not
yet wired to opcua_core (no OpcuaSimulator/OpcuaVariable impl, no server.rs, no client) --
that remaining work is already tracked as op-szmi.4 ("htgr_sim_v1: OPC-UA client +
roundtrip test"), which this issue depends on rather than duplicates. No third OPC-UA
integration exists anywhere in the crate. No new shared-infrastructure design is needed
for piece #4 of op-wqk.22 -- closing this as informational/pointer once op-szmi.4 is
linked.
title: OPC-UA shared layer: confirm already generalized, point at op-szmi.4 for remaining HTGR wiring
